maintenance_led.reason: Revenue is mainly recurring home medical supplies and equipment (diabetes, sleep, wound care, ostomy) delivered to patients, not repair or servicing of installed assets.

publicly_funded.reason: Apria and Byram home care products are largely reimbursed by Medicare, Medicaid and Medicare Advantage, though commercial insurers also pay.

serial_acquirer.reason: Growth is mainly organic through home-based care brands Apria and Byram; the Apria purchase was one large deal.

mission_critical.reason: Patients depend on ongoing sleep, respiratory, diabetes and ostomy supplies and equipment; switching disrupts care, insurer contracts and clinical support.

notes: Government share of revenue is uncertain; it rests on typical Medicare and Medicaid reimbursement for home medical equipment. Owens & Minor's products segment may still be part of the company.
